messages:
Ola (AE): Heads-up 00M bank RFP: Private deploy required. Must preserve original client 5-tuple (no SNAT), provide stable egress IP(s) for allowlisting, and contractual burst capacity (2x baseline for 15m). Any immediate blockers?
Dan (SE): Key tradeoffs: 1) To preserve L4 client IPs we need TGW or direct VPC peering with routes to connector subnets (no SNAT). 2) PrivateLink is easier ops-wise but only preserves identity at L7 via headers (X-Forwarded-For).
Priyanka (NetOps): Ops checklist for customer: allow inbound from connector CIDRs on TCP/443, healthchecks on TCP/80, route entries to connector subnets (TGW/peering). Reserve EIP pool if static egress required; avoid on-demand EIPs due to quotas.
Hector (Solutions Eng): Short security questionnaire blurb: "Redwood Private supports Transit Gateway, VPC peering, and Interface VPC Endpoints. For transport-layer client IP preservation, customers should use TGW or VPC peering and avoid SNAT. Static egress IPs provided via reserved EIP pools or dedicated egress instances. If Interface Endpoints are used, client identity can be forwarded at the application layer via X-Forwarded-For."
M (Customer): Good. Two asks: can you price reserved eip + burst buffer? and can you guarantee burst SLA?
Dan (SE): Ballpark: baseline cluster for ~300 rps ~$10k/mo; reserved EIP + pre-warmed burst buffer adds ~25-35%. Burst SLA only with Dedicated reserved nodes and contract addendum; otherwise best-effort. Legal to finalize.
Priyanka (NetOps): Quick test snippets to validate on your side: traceroute/tcpdump to connector EIP, curl -w "%{time_total}\n" https://<connector-eip>/healthz, and ping MTU test. We'll provide CIDRs and SG examples.
InfraBot: Preflight checklist: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/private-peering-preflight created.
Ola (AE): Next steps: Dan to send a 1-page arch diagram + allowlist by EOD, Hector to draft questionnaire answers, schedule sync Wed 11am PT with customer netsec.
M (Customer): Wed 11am PT works. Thanks all.
